# sogni-client Rust SDK complete agent reference

Crate version: 5.50.0. Compatible with TypeScript 5.50.0 at upstream commit
452e78967a21ab80977c11f16517072d1836405a; hosted protocol 1.0.0-alpha.42.
Repository: https://github.com/morlz/sogni-client-rs. Crate path: `sogni_client`.
Async runtime: Tokio. All public network methods return
`sogni_client::Result<T>`.

Dependency: `sogni-client = "5.50.0"`; disable default features for clients
that do not need wallet signing. Development Git dependency: repository above,
branch dev. Release tags use v<crate-version>.

## Construction and authentication

`SogniClient::builder()` returns `ClientBuilder`.

Builder methods: `app_id`, `app_source`, `attribution`, `network`, `api_key`,
`tokens`, `cookie_auth`, `rest_endpoint`, `socket_endpoint`, `disable_socket`,
`testnet`, `request_timeout`, `connect_timeout`, `defer_socket_start`,
`proxy_url`, `strict_media_destinations`,
`socket_event_subscription`, and async `build`.

Default REST endpoint: `https://api.sogni.ai`.
Default socket endpoint: `wss://socket.sogni.ai`.
Networks: `Network::Fast`, `Network::Relaxed`.

WebSocket clients require an explicit, nonblank `app_id`, trimmed during
construction. Generate it once and persist it across restarts. There is no
random per-start default. `disable_socket(true)` needs no ID, uses `rest-only`
when omitted, and never connects a WebSocket. `defer_socket_start(true)` still
requires a stable app ID because later socket commands can open a connection.

API-key authentication starts automatically. Token authentication accepts the
Authorization value and refresh token; JWT expiry drives refresh through
`/v1/account/refresh-token`. `check_auth` is only for cookie-auth flows.
Username/password authentication requires the default `wallet` feature and is
available through `account.login` or `account.create_account`.

## AccountApi

Methods: `get_nonce`, `login`, `login_with_options`, `create_account`, `logout`,
`me`, `account_balance`, `refresh_balance`, `wallet_balance`,
`validate_username`, `switch_network`, `transaction_history`, `rewards`,
`claim_rewards`, `withdraw`, `deposit`, `approve_token_usage`,
`get_subscription_status`, `get_subscription_usage`, `get_trial_eligibility`,
`set_device_id`, `get_subscription_plans`, `create_subscription_checkout`, and
`create_subscription_portal_session`.

`current_account()` returns a cheap cloneable handle. `snapshot()` is the raw
serializable state. Convenience getters expose username, email, wallet,
balance, subscription, free-Spark lock state, network, and unlimited
entitlement. Versioned socket subscription events remain authoritative over
older in-flight REST refreshes. `subscribe()` emits updates.

## ProjectsApi

Construct requests with `ProjectRequest::image`, `video`, or `audio`. All set
`type`, `modelId`, `positivePrompt`, and default `numberOfMedia=1`. Builder
methods: `param`, `number_of_media`, `steps`, `guidance`, `dimensions`,
`duration`, `fps`, `network`, `asset`, `sam3_prompt`,
`pixal3d_options`, `world_generation_receipt`, and `attribution`.

`MediaSource::Path` performs async file I/O. `MediaSource::bytes` and
`named_bytes` accept memory. `AssetRole` includes starting/control/context
images and video/audio/mask roles. `ReferenceAudioSlot(1..=3)` and
`ReferenceVideoSlot(1..=3)` map MiniMax H3 r2v's numbered, contiguous media
slots. Adding any asset enables its matching wire flag. `Custom` carries a
forward-compatible wire name and whether the media endpoint is required.
`GptImageMask` marks a PNG alpha edit mask in the referenceMask slot.
`Pixal3dLeftView`, `Pixal3dBackView`, and `Pixal3dRightView` use fixed context
slots 1, 2, and 3; subsets retain the named view's slot.

`projects.create(request)` uploads assets, submits `jobRequest`, and returns a
cloneable `Project`. `Project` methods: `id`, `status`, `jobs`, `progress`,
`result_urls`, `snapshot`, `subscribe`, `wait_for_completion`, `cancel`.
`Job` methods: `snapshot`, `id`, `status`, `progress`, `result_url`,
`is_withheld`, `has_result_media`, `subscribe`, `get_result_url`,
`get_result_data`, `enhance`, `enhancement_project`, `media_type`,
`preparation`, `provenance`, `job_index`, `last_frame_url`, and
`get_last_frame_url`.

SAM3: use `ProjectRequest::image("sam3_image_segment_bf16", "")` with
`AssetRole::StartingImage` and `Sam3ImagePrompt`. It forces numberOfMedia=1,
numberOfPreviews=0, and outputFormat=png in both the request and project state.
Points use x/y in [0,1] and Sam3PointLabel::Positive or Negative. Boxes use
x0/y0/x1/y1 in [0,1], with x0<x1 and y0<y1. At least one point, box, or text
prompt is required. Limits: 32 points, 16 boxes, 240 UTF-16 text code units.
Text and points cannot be combined; points allow at most one positive box.
Optional box label defaults to Positive; Negative excludes a text-prompted
instance. Threshold defaults to 0.5. Multimask defaults to true for points;
without points, true fails and false is omitted. apply_mask=true returns an
RGBA source cutout with the mask in alpha. max_instances keeps the top 1–16
selections; omission retains all matches above threshold. Unknown fields fail.

BiRefNet: image model birefnet_image_background_removal_fp16, empty prompt,
and StartingImage. It returns one PNG/no previews; top-level applyMask=true
returns a cutout, default false a matte. SAM3's applyMask is nested instead.

Pixal3D: `ProjectRequest::image("pixal3d_int8_i23d", "")` requires a
starting image. Wire outputFormat is always glb and previews are zero. `job.media_type()` is model;
result URL lookups and recovery use /v1/media/downloadUrl with
contentType=model/gltf-binary. Model artifacts and segmentation masks/cutouts
cannot use image enhancement.
`is_model_artifact_model` recognizes pixal3d_ IDs; the ProjectsApi method
`is_model_artifact_model_id` also accepts advertised media=model for unknown
models. Known pixal3d_ IDs remain artifacts if stale metadata says image.

Multi-view model pixal3d_multiview_int8_i23d uses StartingImage as the front,
plus any named orbit roles above. Left/right refer to the subject's own side.
Both IDs reject generic contextImages. Single-view rejects orbit views;
multi-view rejects templateVariant. Pixal3dGenerationOptions fields:
template_variant (I23dBirefnet, single-view only), texture_size (1024–4096),
mesh_target_faces (5000–700000), normal_map_size (512–2048),
ambient_occlusion_size (256–1024), shape_resolution (1024–1536).
Omit controls for service defaults; shape resolution 1536 is a priced increase
from the default 1024. `.pixal3d_options(...)` emits camelCase wire fields.

`JobProvenance` includes optional sha256, source_image_sha256,
sam_prompt_sha256, mask_rle_sha256, mask_width, mask_height, sam_version,
selection_hash, first_frame_sha256, and last_frame_sha256. Live and recovered
results normalize valid hashes to lowercase; malformed and unknown fields
are omitted from this projection. `jobCompleted` events include provenance
when present, and JobSnapshot serializes it as camelCase.
Mask metadata also exposes mask_box, mask_coverage, mask_detected_count,
mask_returned_count, and mask_selections. Sam3Selection includes optional
score and bounds (wire box), coverage, and included. Bounds use source-normalized
coordinates.

`WorldGenerationReceiptRequest::TargetStill` carries source_image_sha256 and
selection_hash. `Transition` carries first_frame_sha256 and last_frame_sha256.
Receipts serialize inside keyFrames[0]. Applications choose the recipe; the
SDK validates shape/hashes, and the service decides model eligibility and
authorization. No hard-coded model or appSource gate remains in the client.

`JobPreparation` variants: DownloadingAssets, UnloadingModel, LoadingModel.
Model phases carry model, JobModelPhaseStep::{Start,End}, and optional
elapsed_sec. Typed views are available from Job and JobSnapshot; raw fields
remain in JobSnapshot.extra["preparation"] for forward compatibility.

Safety semantics: `is_nsfw && !nsfw_detected` means media was withheld. A
completed result with `nsfw_detected=true` was labeled but delivered.

Discovery/metadata: `wait_for_models`, `get_supported_models`,
`get_model_options`, `get_size_presets`, `get_available_models`,
`get_video_asset_config`, `available_loras`, `get_lora`, `supports_loras`,
`lora_constraints`.

Costs: `estimate_cost` (image), `estimate_video_cost`, `estimate_audio_cost`,
`estimate_enhancement_cost`, and low-level forward-compatible `estimate`.

URLs/uploads: v1 `upload_url`, `download_url`, `media_upload_url`,
`media_download_url`; v2 `image_upload_post`, `media_upload_post`, and
`upload_presigned`.

projects.assets() returns ReusableUploads with upload(&MediaSource), list(),
remove(id), and bind(id, &SavedUploadBinding). upload returns SavedUpload:
id, name, bytes, content_type, state, created_at, expires_at. Binding fields:
project_id, asset_type (wire type), optional id. Normal project creation can
reuse eligible verified private uploads automatically. Continue passing real
files through .asset(); a saved ID is not a replacement file parameter.
Eligibility and verification remain server-owned; account changes invalidate
cached availability. Unavailable saved uploads can fall back before preparation;
transfer/finalization/binding failures surface instead of silently falling back.

Recovery: `sync(reason)` fetches the app-scoped durable snapshot and replays
media project state. `list_projects_elsewhere` is read-only. The SDK invokes
recovery after socket authentication and after an internal receiver lag.
Terminal failed/canceled recovery settles outstanding waiters and unfinished
jobs, preserving existing errors or the server's reason. Completed jobs remain
unchanged. Local timeouts never imply server cancellation.
Worker reassignment retains the same logical Job handle/job_index while its
attempt ID changes. Old-attempt events cannot overwrite new progress/results.
Only explicit restart admission refusals can automatically resend the original
project request; uncertain writes require reconciliation.

## GPT Image and speech controls

GPT IDs: gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2.5-sunburst, gpt-image-2.5-flare.
Custom width/height: 256–3840. Up to 16 ordered context references. A PNG alpha
mask uses AssetRole::GptImageMask or gptImageMaskUrl (URL/PNG data URI), requires
the first reference, and cannot combine both inputs. Data-URI masks are uploaded
as bytes for durable recovery. gptImageQuality accepts low/medium/high and
legacy standard/hd; 2.5 adds xhigh/max. auto quality is rejected.
gptImageBackground accepts opaque/auto; 2.5 adds transparent for PNG/WebP.
gptImageOutputCompression accepts integer 0–100 only with jpg/webp outputFormat.
Set these exact wire names through .param().

Qwen3-TTS IDs: qwen3_tts_1.7b_custom_voice_bf16,
qwen3_tts_1.7b_voice_design_bf16, qwen3_tts_1.7b_voice_clone_bf16.
Use ProjectRequest::audio with the spoken script as prompt. speaker selects a
preset, instruct describes delivery or a designed voice, referenceText is the
exact transcript of referenceAudio. Upload clone audio with AssetRole::ReferenceAudio.
Speech duration follows the script. The serializer preserves speech controls
for service validation rather than maintaining a model allowlist.
Audio ModelOptions.raw includes only advertised controls: speaker options,
instruct {maxLength,required}, referenceText {maxLength}, acceptsReferenceAudio,
requiresReferenceAudio. Speech tiers can omit sampler/scheduler/duration/BPM.
No sampler/scheduler choices means corresponding null wire fields. Discover
individual model capabilities at runtime.

## Video frame behavior

Call `calculate_video_frames(model_id, duration, fps, min, max)`.

- WAN 2.2: generation is fixed at 16 FPS; output FPS may represent later
  interpolation. Frames = rounded(duration * 16) + 1.
- LTX families: generate at requested FPS, then snap to `1 + n*8`.
- MiniMax H3: fixed 24 FPS and `124 + n*17`, clamped to supported limits.
- FlashVSR: rounded(duration * fps), retaining the exact source frame count.
- Other video families: rounded(duration * fps) + 1.

Project creation performs local preflight validation for the current MiniMax
H3, Wan 3, Seedance, and HappyHorse asset/task/duration contracts before any
generation request is submitted.
Wan 3 rejects the retired smartDuration field whenever present, including
false or null. Supply an explicit duration from 2 to 30 seconds.

FastH3 IDs: minimax-h3-fastvideo-int8_{mode}_turbo, with t2v/i2v/flf2v/ia2v/
flfa2v/a2v. Append _2stage for twice the canvas width/height with unchanged
timing and audio. Send a normal H3 canvas (e.g. 672x384, 960x544, 1344x768),
and estimate that canvas with the selected _2stage ID. outputScale is retired
and rejected whenever present, including false/null. _turbo_2stage_720p IDs
are retired and cannot be submitted.

Audio-guide ia2v requires referenceImage + referenceAudio; flfa2v also requires
referenceImageEnd; a2v requires only referenceAudio. Each rejects other upload
roles. Fixed 24fps, 4 steps, guidance 1, and 124+n*17 frames in 124–362, on the
existing H3 32px canvas grid. get_minimax_h3_frames_for_audio_duration(seconds)
returns the smallest covering valid count, clamped to the supported range.
audioStart is a nonnegative offset. Uploaded audio always accompanies output;
generateAudio=false, audioDuration, loras and loraStrengths are rejected.
Empty LoRA arrays are harmless and omitted. Other H3 IDs reject audioStart;
all H3 IDs reject audioDuration.

FlashVSR: FLASHVSR_VIDEO_UPSCALE_MODEL_ID = flashvsr_v1.1_tiny_long_bf16.
Use one video project, empty prompt, ReferenceVideo, upscaleResolution 1080/1440.
It preserves the whole source, its exact frame rate, and audio. Frames/FPS/size
may be omitted for server probing; values supplied must describe the source.
Explicit frames win over duration; duration without frames requires exact FPS.
Fractional rates remain intact. The SDK imposes no clip-length maximum.
detailPreference=stable|sharper; processingSpeed=stable|faster; seed=-1 or an
integer 0–4294967295. Defaults stable/stable/0; steps=1, no interpolation.
Prompts, trims, generation controls, other references, and audio removal fail.
Catalog fields: task=video-upscale, outputResolutions, preservesSourceTiming,
requiresReferenceVideo. Estimates accept sourceWidth/sourceHeight with output
dimensions and exact source timing; the service verifies the uploaded video.

Seedance 2.5 accepts outputFormat=mp4|mov and returnLastFrame=true. Other video
models cannot request MOV or a last-frame export. JobSnapshot exposes
last_frame_url, last_frame_key, output_format. job.last_frame_url() reads the
cached export; job.get_last_frame_url().await refreshes it through artifact=lastFrame.

Use runtime model metadata where possible. Model IDs in docs are illustrative.

## ChatApi

Socket-native non-streaming:

```rust
let result = client.chat.create_completion(&serde_json::json!({
  "model": model_id,
  "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}],
  "think": false
})).await?;
```

Socket-native streaming returns `ChatStream`, which implements
`futures_util::Stream<Item = Result<ChatChunk>>`. `wait(timeout)` returns the
assembled completion; `final_result()` is available after stream closure.
Tool-call argument fragments are assembled by index.

Supported completion wire options include maxTokens/max_tokens, temperature,
topP/top_p, topK/top_k, minP/min_p, repetition/frequency/presence penalties,
stop, tokenType, billingMode, tools, toolChoice/tool_choice, sogniTools,
sogniToolExecution, taskProfile, responseFormat, safeContentFilter, `think`, and
workload attribution.

`think` maps to `chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking`. For structured output,
prefer function tools plus required tool choice. Helpers:
`is_sogni_tool_call` and `parse_tool_call_arguments`.

Hosted REST: `create_hosted_completion`. Direct synchronous hosted tools:
`execute_hosted_tool`. The hosted tool manifest has 27 version-pinned entries;
read through `HostedTools` rather than copying schemas.

Current hosted definitions include generate_speech and upscale_video, plus
FastH3 audio-guide/two-stage and GPT Image 2.5 selectors. These definitions
come from protocol alpha.42. chat.execute_tool_call directly executes six
media tools: generate_image, edit_image, generate_video, sound_to_video,
video_to_video, generate_music. Other tools use hosted chat or durable runs.

Routing helpers: resolve_hosted_tool_model_selector(tool_name, &args),
is_edit_image_model(model_id), get_video_defaults(model_id),
filter_video_models_by_workflow(&models, &workflows), and
select_backbone_model(&models, &BackboneModelOptions). BackboneModelOptions
contains media_type, requested_model, workflows, preferred_model_ids, filter.
Selection uses a compatible explicit model, then preference order, then worker
availability; equal worker counts preserve catalog order. SelectedBackboneModel
exposes model_id, model, selected_by. VideoDefaults contains width/height/fps.

Durable chat: `create_run`, `get_run`, `cancel_run`, `confirm_run_cost`, and
`stream_run_events`. `Idempotency-Key` and workload attribution are propagated.
SSE resume uses `Last-Event-ID`.

Socket chat preserves streams confirmed alive after reconnection. A lost turn
returns a structured retryable error instead of being automatically replayed.
ChatError.retryable() and is_retryable_chat_error(&Error) recognize the public
server_restarting and transport_lost types, also listed in RETRYABLE_CHAT_ERROR_TYPES.

## CreativeWorkflowsApi

`WorkflowStart` accepts exactly one of inline `input` or saved `workflow_id`.
Other fields: `inputs`, `token_type`, `billing_mode`, `app_source`,
`max_estimated_capacity_units`, `confirm_cost`, `media_references`,
`idempotency_key`, `safe_content_filter`, and attribution. Explicit false is
preserved in safe_content_filter on the wire.

Methods: `start`, `list`, `get`, `events`, `stream_events`, `confirm_cost`,
`resume`, `reseed`, `cancel`. Terminal statuses include `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, and `partial_failure`. Waiting reasons are exposed through
`CREATIVE_WORKFLOW_WAITING_REASONS`.

Templates: `workflows.templates.list/get/create/update/delete/fork`.

## Other namespaces

- `ReplayApi`: `write`, `list`, `get`.
- `StatsApi`: `leaderboard`.
- `AnnouncementsApi`: `active`, `dismiss`. Subscribe to `appAlert` at client
  construction when live app alerts are desired.

## Transport, lifecycle, and errors

The shared reqwest client pools HTTP connections, stores cookies, follows a
bounded redirect policy, uses Rustls/native roots, and applies request/connect
timeouts. The WebSocket sends JSON envelopes with a base64-encoded JSON `data`
field, normalizes `jobID`/`imgID` to uppercase, pings periodically, and applies
capped jittered exponential reconnect delay.

SSE APIs return `SseStream`; each `SseEvent` includes event, parsed data, id,
and raw frame. Consumers own endpoint-specific terminal handling and reconnect
policy.

Error variants: `Api`, `Project`, `Chat`, `InvalidInput`, `Protocol`,
`Transport`, `Timeout`, `Closed`, `Json`, `Url`, `Http`, `Io`.
`is_subscription_limit_error` recognizes the stable public subscription error
contract.

Never embed secrets. Credential `Debug` output is redacted. Keep one client
alive, explicitly `close()` it during shutdown, and never interpret a local
timeout as server cancellation.
